title: Content Design Starts With a User Need
intro: Start from who needs to do what, and why. Then decide whether it needs words at all.

topics.title: Content Design Starts With a User Need

learn.title: The format
learn.text:
**As a…** who, by their relationship to the task.
**I need to…** a task.
**So that…** why it matters.

As a carer, I need to get financial help, so that I can keep looking after the person I care for.

try.explain: Name the role that makes the need specific.

learn.title: No solution inside
learn.text:
A need describes a goal, not a tool.

“I need to use the benefits calculator” justifies a tool. “I need to know how much I could get” is a need.

try.q: Which is a real user need?
options: I need to know how much I could get
I need to use the benefits calculator
I need a PDF of the benefit rules
I need a chatbot to answer me

learn.title: Acceptance criteria
learn.text:
What must be true for the need to be met.

For the carer: understand the allowance, check eligibility, apply, know the amount.

Record each need with its criteria, evidence and owner.

options: What must happen for the need to be met
How long the page should be

learn.title: Need, plan, write, maintain
learn.text:
**Identify** the need with evidence.
**Plan** the amount, format and place, and check for duplicates.
**Write** clearly.
**Maintain** or archive.

try.explain: Sometimes the answer is a sentence in the UI, or removing a page.

test.q: Which verb fits a user need best?
test.explain: Needs are tasks; “be aware of” only if it serves a task.

test.q: When is “understand” acceptable in a need?
options: When the “so that” shows a task
With criteria, evidence and an owner
test.explain: So content can be checked and retired.

options: What does someone need to do?
How should this page be worded?
How long can this page be?

test.q: A need is met elsewhere already. What do you do?
options: Link to it from every page
